# Road safety audit: FIDRT 20250526_video

Source: SAM 3.1 tiled video tracking (Meta Model API). Observed 10.0 min; 476 two-wheelers, 368 vehicles. Traffic control: Signalized; right turns signal-controlled: no.

Conflicts: 176 interacting pairs with PET ≤ 1.5 s or TTC ≤ 1.5 s (117 PET, 59 TTC). Each pair is counted once, by PET when it has one.

Hotspots are 15 m cells ranked by the lower bound of the exact Poisson 95% interval on conflicts per 1,000 road users through the cell (at least 2 conflicts). These are surrogate measures from a short observation, not crash frequencies.

## Hotspot 1 at (22.5, -22.5) m

14 conflicts among 123 road users: 113.8 per 1,000 (95% CI 62.2–191.0). Dominant: 6 turning two-wheeler – two-wheeler conflicts (min PET 0.4 s; movements 2 left, 4 u-turn, 2 right, 1 unknown, 1 through).

Muse Spark reviewed the video of the 3 most severe of these: 2 rated real conflicts, 1 not (2 with visible braking or swerving).

Illustration: Dedicated Left- and Right-Turn Lanes at Intersections (hotspot1_20250526_video.png). SAM 3.1 check for 'arrow road marking' in the hotspot: found (covered share 0.010 before, 0.110 after). AI-generated; not an engineering design.

| FHWA Proven Safety Countermeasure | CMF Clearinghouse ID | CMF | Crash reduction | Rating | Crash type | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dedicated Left- and Right-Turn Lanes at Intersections | 276 | 0.74 | 26% | 4★ | Angle | no two-wheeler-specific crash type exists in the CMF Clearinghouse |
| Reduced Left-Turn Conflict Intersections | 10870 | 0.61 | 39% | 5★ | Angle | no two-wheeler-specific crash type exists in the CMF Clearinghouse |

panel.memo:
# Memo: Traffic Engineer

## Observed

In 599.9 observed units, 176 conflicts were recorded at a Signalized site. Rank 1 had 14 events, rate 113.8 per 1000 with ci95 [62.2, 191.0]; its dominant turning two-wheeler/two-wheeler pattern had 6 events and min PET 0.4. Video review checked 3, finding 2 real and 2 evasive braking conflicts on intersecting paths. Rank 2 had 9 events, rate 95.7 per 1000 with ci95 [43.8, 181.8], but only 1 of 3 reviewed was real, converging in the channelized slip lane. Rank 3 had 12 events, but 0 of 3 reviewed were real; PET 0.0 reflected tracking artefacts and queued stopped vehicles, so do not treat it as a hotspot.

## Consider first

Evaluate CMF 276 first at Rank 1: it is the offset left-turn lane treatment, CMF 0.74 and CRF 26.0, matching Signalized Angle All conflicts where left and u_turn movements occur. Evaluate CMF 10870 as a more comprehensive alternative: CMF 0.6108 and CRF 38.92 for converting to a median U-turn intersection. Neither accepted CMF addresses Rank 2's right-turn slip-lane movement, so that location needs separate design review rather than these left-turn treatments.

## Limits

These are surrogate measures from a short observation, not crash predictions. Applicability is uncertain because no two-wheeler-specific crash type exists. A qualified traffic engineer must review any design.
